scores.name: The Herald Gazette
scores.verdict: WINNER. Only design where a zero-click lurker gets 100% of the value — scroll a thread like a newspaper. Best luddite story (10/10 justified), best component headroom (all messages ≤24/40 vs the Board's 37/40), the snarky sports-desk voice is the wow and needs no LLM, and Pin-to-Fridge is the one tasteful public-write escape valve. Also the fastest thing to post live as a mockup TODAY: 7 hardcoded fixture-driven messages through the existing spikes/menu-v2/post.py + charts.py. Its real costs (back-issue snapshots, week-flip 7-message edit serialization, troll-build heuristic fallbacks) are all deferrable past the mockup.

scores.name: Herald Match Browser
scores.verdict: Technical best-in-class, second overall. The only design with zero constraint violations found — every component count re-verified correct, hero select exactly 25, fully-stateless custom_id grammar makes it restart- and token-expiry-proof with no session store, and it pre-solves every V2 gotcha (defer(6)+PATCH @original for modal submits and attachment swaps, 3,800-char degrade guard). Loses on wow: the public channel shows a 5-component kiosk and all delight hides in per-user ephemerals; L0 filters-first entry reads as a form, which luddites bounce off.

scores.name: The Match Board (Command Deck)
scores.verdict: Elegant single-artifact concept but running hot on both caps: 37/40 components in BROWSE with zero headroom, and a plausible 4,000-char breach (~3,500-3,850) if select option text counts toward the pool — its own risks section admits this is unverified. Shared last-click-wins state is the luddite trap: one user's click morphs the Board under another user's eyes mid-read ('feels haunted' is their phrase, and correct). Its factoid engine, emoji-slug budget discipline, and GROUPED drill rows are the best subsystems in the field.

scores.name: The Herald Reel
scores.verdict: Highest raw wow (media-first Netflix poster wall) but weakest fit for a TODAY prototype: the Pillow poster compositor does not exist in the spike (only matplotlib charts do), every page flip re-uploads 4 PNGs so every interaction is a deferred multi-second edit, and it inherits the Board's shared-public-state race. Spec arrived truncated mid-MESSAGE-3, so detail view, budget, and risks are unverifiable — scored with an uncertainty penalty. Verified portions are cap-legal (27/40, 33/40, 7/10 attachments) with two minor spec errors.

scores.name: Design 6 (not received)
scores.verdict: NOT SCORED — absent from the truncated prompt, no source file found in the repo or scratchpad.

steals: FROM THE MATCH BOARD (3): (1) The rule-based factoid third line with its priority ladder (15+ death feeder → 25+ kill player → kills/min record → biggest comeback → blank) — this is the cheapest charm-per-line in any design; use it on every Gazette board entry and every browser list row. (2) Short app-emoji slug discipline (h_pa, i_bfury) plus the 3,600-char render-time guard with staged degradation (truncate factoid → drop item emojis → hero names as text) — make this the shared render layer for ALL surfaces; it is load-bearing math, not style. (3) GROUPED mode with drill buttons (group by hero/day/length, aggregate rows like 'Pudge — 61 matches · bloodiest 97 kills · won 44%', drill sets the filter and returns to flat) — a genuinely luddite-friendly browse pattern nobody else has. FROM HERALD MATCH BROWSER (3): (1) The fully-stateless custom_id grammar (hb|action|d|u|k|h|s|p|m|x, ~50/100 chars) — filters, sort, page, match id all in every id; bot restarts and 15-minute token expiry become non-events and no Postgres session table is needed. Adopt wholesale. (2) Per-user ephemeral sessions edited in place via type 7 — the correct answer to the shared-state race that dogs both the Board and the Reel; ten users browse in parallel with zero contention and zero channel spam. (3) The always-valid interaction paths: defer(6) + PATCH @original for modal submits and any attachment swap (listing only the new file to auto-drop the old chart), plus the 14-option networth chart-mode select (team lead / all 10 / cores / supports / per-player). FROM THE HERALD REEL (2): (1) The Pillow poster composite — but for exactly ONE image, the front-page featured match (5v5 portraits + scoreline + burned-in networth sparkline), rendered once at print time and cached; all the wow, none of the per-page-flip upload churn. (2) MediaGallery-as-grid for a 'Week in Charts' page (kills-by-day bars, duration histogram, shame-quadrant scatter) — the multi-item gallery is the most underused V2 primitive in the other designs.
constraint_violations: PROCESS: Designs 5 and 6 were never received — the prompt's JSON truncates mid-Design-4 (inside The Herald Reel's 'MESSAGE 3: MATCH POSTER' layout); no full source file exists in the repo or scratchpad. This judgment covers 4 of 6. PER DESIGN — Match Board: no hard overcount (BROWSE recounts to exactly 37/40) but zero headroom, and a probable 4,000-char breach in BROWSE if select option labels/descriptions count toward the pool (25-option hero select with descriptions adds ~1,200 chars onto a ~2,300 base → ~3,500-3,850; the spec sheet's '4000 chars combined across all component text' suggests they DO count) — must be empirically verified first thing in the spike; the modal-submit→type-7 path is the one fragile interaction (fallback specified, ship the fallback). Herald Match Browser: no violations found — all counts, option counts (25/14/8/10), and custom_id lengths verified legal; the L3a Players screen at ~3,400 chars makes its 3,800 degrade guard mandatory, which the design itself states. Herald Gazette: no component overcounts (max 24/40, selects 13 and 25); soft gaps — the type-6 defer on week-flip only covers the front-page message, the other 6 thread messages need bot-token PATCHes serialized against channel edit rate limits; the back-issue select is nearly empty given ~1-week DB retention unless weekly snapshots are persisted; Comeback City pages 2/3 component layout (featured MediaGallery kept or dropped?) is unspecified. Herald Reel: filter select claims 16 options but enumerates 15 (trivial); '✖️ Clear all filters' as a selectable option inside a min 0 / max 3 multi-select is self-contradictory (user can select clear + two filters simultaneously — needs server-side precedence rule or a separate button); 4 poster PNGs re-uploaded per page flip forces a deferred edit on every navigation; verified portions cap-legal (Gallery 27/40, Calendar 33/40, 7/10 attachments) but detail view, budget, and risks are unverifiable due to truncation. ALL FOUR received designs correctly preserve the pull-only constraint (mention-triggered creation, edits never ping, no unprompted posts).
definitive_recommendation: Build 'The Gazette front-end on the Browser back-end' — a clear hybrid emerges. SPINE (from Gazette): one thread per ISO week, mention-triggered, containing the 7-message edition (Front Page, Longest Wars, Bloodbaths, Feeder Hall of Fame, Comeback City w/ inline chart, Troll Builds, Classifieds), all pages edited in place, snarky sports-desk voice, Pin-to-Fridge as the only user-initiated public write. This wins because the primary audience is lurkers in a non-technical server: zero clicks yields full entertainment, and it is the fastest credible live mockup today (post.py + charts.py + fixtures already exist — hardcode Front Page + Bloodbaths + Feeders + one comeback chart and post it this afternoon). PLUMBING (from Browser): every Full Story button, Classifieds browse, and hero spotlight opens a per-user EPHEMERAL drill-down (filters → list → match card → Players/Networth/Items) using the stateless custom_id grammar — this simultaneously kills the shared-state race, the restart-amnesia problem, and the need for any session table, and it replaces Gazette's thinner ephemeral browse with the field's best-specified one. SHARED RENDER LAYER (from Board): the rule-based factoid ladder on every list row, short emoji slugs, and the 3,600-char guard with staged degradation, enforced by a single pre-send counter used by every surface. GARNISH (from Reel): one cached Pillow poster composite for the front-page featured match only, plus a Week-in-Charts ephemeral using a 4-item MediaGallery. Day-1 spike priorities, in order: (1) empirically test whether select option text counts toward the 4,000-char limit (decides how rich the Classifieds selects can be), (2) verify defer(6)+PATCH @original with attachments on the installed discord.py/raw REST path, (3) post the 3-message static Gazette mockup to #replays.
